chunk_map.heading: 1. Treat CI as feedback into the loop, not a gate to pass
2. Fan out review; converge on the pattern
3. Tier by blast radius. Make the Tier-1 case on your own PRs
Stripe bets on the sandbox, not the slice
4. Eval latency is part of the loop
Cherny pairs a fast check with a slow one
5. Skills don't just live in your kit. Promote them into the CI surface
The skill catalogue scales: plan time to company-wide
6. Get out fast. Learn from real customers safely
Agents need the outer loop's signal too
Where this fits in your AE101 arc

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest candidates, both resolve within their own chunk: chunk 3 line 21 "A single reviewer reading 30 agent-drafted PRs a day skims. The best refuse the trade." — 'the trade' is the implicit speed/thoroughness trade-off named in the immediately preceding sentence of the SAME chunk, one clear candidate, not vague-with-full-history. Chunk 5 header (line 35) "Stripe bets on the sandbox, not the slice" names 'the slice' before its own body explains it (line 37 'auto-merging the lowest-risk slice'), but the explanation lands later in the SAME chunk, not a future one — header-then-explanation within one slide, not a forward reference to a later slide. Checked all 14 chunks for never-named or vague-with-full-history referents: none found. Collective callback in the closer (chunk 12, line 85, 'These engineers run the same loop') resolves against every practitioner named across the file, which the sequential read holds by that point.

Closest candidate, chunk 12 (line 85, current body): "The loop at your desk is the one this training closed: [...] These engineers run the same loop; they've been at it longer." Names the referent by content ('the loop', 'this training', 'these engineers') not by file position ('the opening lecture said'), and functions as the closer summing the whole file against the training arc — the explicitly carved-out case, not a violation. Grepped the body for 'opening lecture|earlier module|prior module|the prework|see below|above|below|further down|at the top of|coming up|in this module': only match is line 5 'None require permission from above to start trying' (idiomatic, hierarchical 'above', not a file-position pointer). No cross-file positional callback found anywhere.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Chunk 0 line 5 (module-flag branch): "Two sessions of the same task, gap diagnosis, a second skill in `~/.claude/skills/`, one rule cut from `./CLAUDE.local.md`." Verified against the current M6 files: `curriculum/trainings/agentic-engineering-101/spot-gaps-build-the-loop.md` line 14 "- **Diagnose** the gaps two sessions of the same task surface, and read where each belongs: memory, sharper verifier, or new skill", line 15 "- **Cut** one rule from `./CLAUDE.local.md` the diagnosis killed", line 25 "You walk in holding two sessions of the same task."; `curriculum/exercises/spot-gaps-build-the-loop.md` line 9 "diff two sessions of the same task", line 37 "Two sessions of the same task were the first real stress-test of `./CLAUDE.local.md`." All three named beats (two sessions, gap diagnosis, rule cut) exist in the current module + exercise. 'a second skill' is one of the module's own three gap-destinations (memory / sharper verifier / new skill), not a guarantee every student's diagnosis lands there — but this is a documented, deliberate cross-file convention, not an invented beat: `curriculum/trainings/agentic-engineering-101/autumn-gaps.md` lines 764-766 independently confirms 'Two address a reader who has shipped a second skill at module 6: `skill-stacking.md:165` opens "You shipped a second skill in M6."' — a sibling supplementary asserts the identical assumption, so this is house convention already reconciled, not a dead reference this file invented alone.

Closest candidate, chunk 1 (shortest chunk, lines 7-10): header + one three-sentence paragraph carrying a complete, self-standing claim ('A failing CI run is signal. About which memory rule should have caught the mistake upstream... Each red build sharpens the next session.'). Not a wait-state or single context-dependent bullet. Checked all 14 chunks: every one carries at least one full paragraph plus (for the numbered-move chunks) a named practitioner example or a 'Try this Monday' action — none is orphaned.

Chunk 4 header (line 29): "3. Tier by blast radius. Make the Tier-1 case on your own PRs." Chunk 4's own content (lines 29-34) delivers the tiering definition and Intercom's stats, but never delivers the header's second clause — no action or guidance for the reader to 'make the case on your own PRs' appears until chunk 5's 'Try this Monday' (line 41), under an unrelated-sounding header ('Stripe bets on the sandbox, not the slice') that is actually framed around Stripe's CONTRASTING sandbox-based bet, not tiering. Compared against the file's other five move headers: each of Move 1 (line 7), Move 2 (line 19, both clauses fulfilled same-chunk via 'Read the pattern across findings' + Cloudflare's coordinator), Move 4 (line 43), Move 5 (line 55, 'Promote them into the CI surface' fulfilled same-chunk via AGENTS.md/rules-files/pre-commit-hooks), and Move 6 (line 69, both clauses fulfilled same-chunk) either carry a single descriptive clause or fulfill every clause within their own chunk. Move 3 alone bundles an imperative promise into its header and defers it to a differently-topicked chunk — an outlier against the file's own pattern, not a contradiction of chunk 4's content, but a promise the chunk itself does not keep.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Either fold a 'make the case' action into chunk 4 itself (mirroring how Move 5's imperative clause is fulfilled in its own chunk), or trim the header to 'Tier by blast radius' and let chunk 5's Try-this-Monday stand on its own without an unclaimed promise pointing at it.

rules_evaluated.evidence: Checked all sub-items against the body. (1) 'Not X. Not Y. Z.' banned construction: grepped 'Not [A-Za-z][^.]*\.' — one hit, line 31 'Not all PRs deserve the same gate.', a single negation, not the triple shape. (2) Anaphora/epistrophe triple: line 9 'About which memory rule should have caught the mistake upstream. About which verifier was too soft. About which skill ran on auto-pilot when it should have paused.' — three legs, but each names a genuinely distinct concrete diagnostic target (rule / verifier / skill, mirroring the module's own three gap-destinations) — the third leg carries new concrete content, which is the rule's own stated pass condition, not the intensifying-repetition it bans. (3) Self-grading superlatives: grepped 'one of the most|most useful|most valuable|most important|game.?chang|revolutioniz' — zero hits in the body; 'the best' is used as a repeated topic-sentence device describing external practitioners ('the best engineers running it'), never grading this training's own content; line 51's '2-3x's the quality' is Cherny's own cited claim (accept-noted CAVEAT source), not the curriculum praising itself. (4) Number + own retraction: checked every stat in the body (52%→80%, 110,000/44,000, 19.2%/14.6min/75.8min/86%, 1,000+/week, 131,246/48,095/5,169/3m39s/0.6%, 10 minutes) — none is paired with a hedge/retraction phrase. (5) Abstraction-noun stacks: grepped for compound-abstraction patterns — none found; closest is line 63 'the same shape of artifact', which resolves concretely against the immediately preceding chunk's AGENTS.md/rules-files/pre-commit-hooks, not a floating abstraction. (6) Empty-leg verb triplets: grepped 'It [a-z]+s\. It [a-z]+s\. It [a-z]+s' — zero hits.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Internal dialect never lands on a slide.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Grepped the banned-term list ('surface as noun'|firing|compendium|forcing function|\bbeat\b|\bmood\b|Connections) against the body: zero genuine hits. The one \bbeat\b match (line 25 'specialized agents beat monolithic prompting') is the ordinary verb 'outperform', not the training-design noun. 'surface' appears twice in ordinary engineering sense — line 31 'different review surfaces' and the chunk-8 header 'the CI surface' (both analogous to 'attack surface', not the authoring-vocabulary noun the rule bans). 'the loop', 'gap diagnosis', 'packaging' are this training's own arc-earned spine vocabulary from M4-M6, not maintainer/repo dialect — in scope for §1's arc-earned carve-out, out of scope for §8.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Listed every bolded span in the body (grep '\*\*[^*]+\*\*' over lines 1-105) and assigned each to its chunk. Budget is ≤1 bolded element per slide for ordinary narrative (no menu/lookup-surface carve-out applies here: this is a sequential essay meant to be read once — 'Take-home reading', 'Read after you've shipped your second skill' — not a scanned reference table the reader consults mid-question; per §9's own scope test, 'a reference page's narrative preamble is still narrative,' and this whole file is that narrative). Six of the 14 chunks exceed the budget: chunk 2 'Two proofs the loop compounds' (lines 11-18) has THREE — line 13 '**Klaassen at Every**', line 15 '**Cursor's Bugbot**', line 17 '**Try this Monday.**'; chunk 3 'Fan out review' has two — line 23 '**Cloudflare engineering**', line 27 '**Try this Monday.**'; chunk 5 'Stripe bets on the sandbox' has two — line 37 '**Stripe**', line 41 '**Try this Monday.**'; chunk 7 'Cherny pairs a fast check' has two — line 51 '**Cherny on Claude Code**', line 53 '**Try this Monday.**'; chunk 9 'skill catalogue scales' has THREE — line 63 '**Larson at Imprint**', line 65 '**Charles runs Ramp's Dojo**', line 67 '**Try this Monday.**'; chunk 11 'Agents need the outer loop's signal too' has THREE — line 77 '**Majors at Honeycomb**', line 79 '**Wolff on the Claude Code team**', line 81 '**Try this Monday.**'. Neither the practitioner-name bolds nor the recurring 'Try this Monday.' are named laws/governors/coined terms/checklist-item names in the rule's sense — they read as attribution styling and a recurring action-cue, which is narrative/recognition-beat prose the rule says gets no bold. By contrast, chunks 4, 6, 8, 10, 12 correctly carry ≤1 bold each, and sibling supplementaries (`workflow-composition-lineages.md`, `the-context-ceiling.md`, checked this session) reserve bold for genuine short coined-move handles ('Start clean.', 'Route by complexity, not price.') or the 'Read:' mode-word, never a per-paragraph name lead — confirming this file's pattern is the outlier, not house style. Flagging as a rule question alongside the finding: if the maintainer reads 'Try this Monday.' as an intentional recurring widget-handle (like 'Read:' in the menu carve-out), the practitioner-name bolds still push every one of these six chunks over budget on their own.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Pick one bolded handle per chunk — most naturally the recurring 'Try this Monday.' action-cue — and drop the practitioner-name bolding to plain text; where two practitioners share one chunk (9, 11), either accept two bolds as this chunk's genuine content or consider a '##' split so each practitioner gets its own budget.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Slide size — 210 words / 6 bullets, and the cap is machine-checked.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Ran `node scripts/check-slide-size.js --file curriculum/trainings/agentic-engineering-101/supplementary/how-the-best-do-ci-cd.md --report` this session → 'oversized: 1' — 'how-the-best-do-ci-cd.md:89 [12 bullets] ## Sources'. The Sources chunk (lines 89-105) carries 12 citation bullets against the 6-bullet ceiling (150 words, within the word cap). Checked the maintainer block (lines 106-165) for a `**Slide size accepted:** ## Sources — <reason>` escape hatch: none present. A corpus precedent exists for exactly this shape: `curriculum/trainings/agentic-engineering-101/supplementary/the-context-ceiling.md` splits its 12 citations into two headed sub-sections ('## Sources: quality and craft', '## Sources: cost and other drivers'), 6 bullets each, verified clean by the same checker this session — the established fix for an over-length Sources list is a split, not an accept-note.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Split '## Sources' into two headed sub-lists (e.g. by the practice each half of the piece covers, or first-half/second-half of the six moves), 6 bullets each, mirroring `the-context-ceiling.md`'s precedent — or add a maintainer `**Slide size accepted:**` note if a single flat list is preferred for this file.
